title: A protocol for selection in mice of highly metastatic ovarian cancer cell with omental tropism
protocol: Expand the OC cells labeled with luciferase in complete DMEM/F12 medium.
Collect the OC cells at 80%-90% confluence for inoculation.
Prewarm the culture medium, PBS and trypsin-EDTA solution at room temperature for 30 min before operation.
Remove the medium in the culture dishes and gently rinse the cells with PBS.
Add 2 ml trypsin-EDTA solution and gently shake the flasks.
Allow enzymatic reaction for 30 s–60 s, optimizing time to reduce cell viability impact.
Add 2 ml complete medium, gently suspend the cells.
Mix all cell suspensions in a new centrifuge tube.
Calculate total number of cells: Total = cell concentration (determined by a cell counter after 0.4% trypan blue staining) × volume.
After a 300 × g centrifugation at room temperature for 5 min, discard the supernatant and obtain the cell pellet.
Wash the cells with PBS.
Resuspend the cells in 1 mL of serum-free medium.
Calculate the total number of viable cells.
Dilute the cell suspension with serum-free medium to a concentration of 1–3 × 10^7/mL in a new 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Keep the tube on ice during transportation.
Inoculate the mice within 1 hour.
Sterilize all materials and equipment using 75% ethanol.
Perform a 30 min ultraviolet irradiation in a superclean bench.
Mix the cell suspension before each extraction.
Disinfect the scapular area of the mouse skin with 75% ethanol.
Wait for the ethanol to dry out.
Inject the cell suspension subcutaneously.
Use BALB/c Nude mice for inoculation with most human OC cell lines.
Use C57BL/6N mice for inoculation with ID8 cells.
For PDX derived from primary cells and cell lines with poor tumorigenicity, use mice with higher levels of immunodeficiency such as NOD-SCIDs or NSG.
Ensure there is no fluid leak during inoculation procedures.
Return the mice to their original cages if they do not exhibit any significant discomfort after inoculation.
Measure tumor diameters when subcutaneous tumors can be observed using a slide caliper.
Calculate tumor volume using the formula Volume = length × width × width / 2.
Euthanize the mouse by cervical dislocation under isoflurane anesthesia when the subcutaneous tumor reaches approximately 0.5 cm3 in volume.
Place the mouse in a prone position and disinfect the mouse skin with 75% ethanol.
Lift and cut the skin in the middle line of the tumor surface for further tissue block preparation.
Dissociate the tumor from the mouse.
Place the tumor in sterile PBS solution at 4°C.
If transplantations cannot be started immediately, keep the tumor in pre-cooled serum-free culture medium at 4°C and transplant within 24 hours.
Remove the tumor capsule with forceps and scissors.
Wash the tumor with cold PBS three times.
Check the tumor carefully to identify sections with better vitality (without bleeding or necrosis).
Obtain 3-4 pieces of tumor tissue from these sections.
Place the selected tissues into a new dish containing fresh cold PBS.
Cut the selected tumor tissues into small tissue-blocks with a maximum diameter of no more than 1 mm.
Wash the tissue blocks with fresh PBS three times.
Keep the tissue blocks in pre-cooled serum-free culture medium at 4°C.
Transplant the tissue blocks to mice within 4 hours.
Disinfect the surfaces of all objects with 75% ethanol spray.
Irradiate disinfected objects with UV light for 30 minutes.
Open the surgical kit on a clean bench.
Cover the operating platform with a sterile operational towel.
Place sterile surgical instruments and objects on the platform.
Set the gas flow of induction cage at 1.5 L/min.
Set the concentration of isoflurane in the induction cage to 2.5%.
Weigh the mice and place them in the induction cage.
Wait for the mice to be fully anesthetized.
Modify the gas flow of the respiratory mask to 0.75 L/min.
Keep the mouse anesthetized by isoflurane through the respiratory mask after placing it on the right side.
Anesthetize all three mice simultaneously in the induction cage.
Open the abdominal cavity.
Disinfect the skin of its left abdomen with 75% ethanol.
Lift the skin at the lowest point with curved ophthalmic forceps and make a 0.4–0.8 cm incision with ophthalmic scissors.
Search for a fat pad sized approximately 0.3 cm × 0.4 cm under the abdominal incision near the spine side.
Gently grip the edge of the fat pad with micro forceps and slowly pull it outside.
Place the mouse under the stereomicroscope.
Open the ovarian bursa.
Gently grab the capsular membrane surrounding the ovary along the borderline of the ovarian bursa and the adipose tissue with micro forceps.
Make an incision in the ovarian bursa with a micro scissor whose size can just match or is slightly smaller than the transplanting tissue-block.
Insert a tissue block into the ovarian bursa with micro forceps, and push it deeply into the bursa as much as possible.
Close the incision with a 7-0 suture.
Gently place the fat pad back to the abdominal cavity.
Close the abdominal cavity with a 5-0 suture.
Clean and disinfect the wound with 75% ethanol.
Turn off the gas flow of mask and wait for the mouse to awaken from the anesthesia.
Return the mouse back to the cages.
Prepare the IVIS and the luciferase substrate working solution.
Initiate the IVIS and set the imaging mode to bioluminescence.
Disinfect the imaging room with 75% ethanol and UV irradiation.
Thaw the luciferase substrate working solution at room temperature or in a 37°C incubator while protecting it from light.
Transport the mice to the imaging room in sterile cages.
Initiate the gas anesthesia system.
Set the gas flow of induction cage at 1.5 L/min, concentration of isoflurane at 2.5%, and oxygen pressure at 0.1 MPa.
Put the mice into the anesthesia induction cage 4 minutes prior to the injection time.
Wait for the mice to be fully anesthetized.
Weigh the mice and calculate the D-luciferin dosage for each mouse.
Mix the D-luciferin solution at a concentration of 15 mg/mL.
Intraperitoneally inject the D-luciferin solution into the mice at a dose of 150 mg/kg (10 μL/g).
Allow the mice to metabolize for 15 minutes before imaging.
Set the gas flow of the imaging chamber to 0.5 L/min when it is time to image.
Place the mouse in the imaging chamber and acquire the image.
Close the isoflurane flow after successful imaging.
Allow the mouse to wake up on a heat pad.
Return the mouse to its cage.
Euthanize the mouse by cervical dislocation under isoflurane anesthesia when peritoneal metastasis is observed.
Lay the mouse on a piece of sterile gauze.
Disinfect the whole abdominal skin of the mouse with 75% ethanol.
Make a horizontal “H” shaped incision to expose the abdominal organs.
Check the left ovary to confirm tumor formation.
Search the omentum between the stomach and the spleen.
Dissociate the omentum and wash it with PBS three times.
Soak the omentum in 150 μg/mL D-luciferin solution in a 60 mm dish.
Incubate the soaked omentum at 37°C for 2–3 min.
Put the dish into the imaging chamber to conduct ex vivo imaging.
Determine tissue areas with strong bioluminescent signals based on the image result.
Harvest parts of omental tissue indicated by strong signals.
Remove bleeding or necrosis sections from harvested tissues.
Obtain tumor tissue blocks for orthotopic transplantation to mice of the next passage.
Transplant tissue-blocks obtained into the ovary bursas of passage 2 mice.
Maintain and process the omentum tissues according to steps 23 to 58.
Wait for the formation of peritoneal metastasis.
Conduct two more cycles of in vivo selection until passage 3 mice.
Isolate HM cells from omental metastasis in a sterile setting.
Culture isolated HM cells ex vivo.
Obtain the omentum from the passage 3 mouse as previously described.
Wash the omentum with PBS three times.
Cut the tissue into pieces of 0.1 mm³ in size.
Prepare collagenase type 1 working solution by adding 200 μL of 1% collagenase type 1 solution in 1800 μL of serum-free medium at a final concentration of 1 mg/mL.
Add 2 mL collagenase type 1 working solution and incubate the tube on a thermostat shaker at 37°C for 1 h.
Add 2 mL fresh medium to dilute the enzyme.
Mix the suspension and infiltrate with a 40 μm cell filter.
Obtain the precipitation through a 200 × g centrifugation at room temperature for 5 min.
Resuspend the precipitation in 5 mL complete DMEM/F12 medium and seed into a 25 cm² culture flask.
Wash HM cells with PBS after 24 h of incubation at 37°C.
Add fresh culture medium to HM cells.
Observe adherent cells under an inverted microscope.
Change the culture medium every three days.
Passage cells at 85%–90% confluence.
